Primary Benefits: Reduces pores, controls oil, fades hyperpigmentation, strengthens skin barrier
Side Effects: Mild flushing at >5% in sensitive skin
Key Interactions: Synergistic with zinc; do NOT mix with pure Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) at same step — wait 10–15 mins
Notes: One of the most well-studied skincare actives. 5% most common; 10% for advanced users

Primary Benefits: Reduces fine lines, boosts collagen, fades dark spots, treats acne
Side Effects: Dryness, peeling, redness, photosensitivity (initial weeks)
pH Range: Above 5.5 is ideal; unstable in high pH
Key Interactions: Do NOT combine with AHAs/BHAs same step; avoid with benzoyl peroxide; pair with barrier support
Notes: Start 2–3x/week; introduce slowly. Retinaldehyde is a stronger precursor

Primary Benefits: Deep and surface hydration, plumps skin, reduces appearance of fine lines
Side Effects: Rarely causes irritation; can dehydrate if no moisturizer on top in dry climates
Skin Types: All skin types, especially Dry and Dehydrated
Key Interactions: Pairs well with ceramides, glycerin, niacinamide
Notes: Look for multi-weight HA (high + low molecular weight) for layered hydration

Primary Benefits: Unclogs pores, reduces blackheads, anti-inflammatory, treats acne
Side Effects: Dryness, over-exfoliation, stinging on broken skin
Key Interactions: Do NOT pair with retinol or strong AHAs in same step; pH-dependent — apply before products above pH 5
Notes: Oil-soluble — penetrates sebum in pores. 0.5–2% OTC; 2% BHA in Paula's Choice is benchmark

Primary Benefits: Resurfaces skin texture, fades PIH, brightens dull skin, boosts collagen
Side Effects: Stinging, redness, photosensitivity (always use SPF)
Key Interactions: Do NOT mix with retinol same step; avoid with strong BHAs for beginners; pair with SPF next morning
Notes: Smallest AHA molecule — deepest penetration. 5–10% for OTC; 20–70% for professional peels

Primary Benefits: Gentle exfoliation, hydrating, brightening, improves texture
Side Effects: Mild stinging; gentler than glycolic
Skin Types: Sensitive, Dry, Mature, Beginners to AHAs
Key Interactions: Good starter AHA; combine with ceramides post-use; avoid vitamin C same step
Notes: Larger molecule than glycolic — milder. Also a humectant

Primary Benefits: Brightens skin, fades dark spots, boosts collagen, protects from UV damage
Side Effects: Instability at wrong pH; tingling on sensitive skin; can cause irritation at high %
Skin Types: All skin types; especially Dull, Hyperpigmentation-prone
Key Interactions: Avoid with niacinamide (wait 10–15 min); do NOT mix with retinol; pair with Vitamin E for synergy
Notes: Highly unstable — look for L-ascorbic acid or more stable derivatives (ascorbyl glucoside, MAP)

Primary Benefits: Restores skin barrier, retains moisture, reduces sensitivity
Side Effects: Very rare; generally extremely well tolerated
Skin Types: All types; especially Dry, Sensitive, Eczema-prone
Key Interactions: Pairs with cholesterol and fatty acids for complete barrier repair (3:1:1 ratio ideal); combine with hyaluronic acid
Notes: Ceramide 1, 3, 6-II are most effective. CeraVe popularized ceramides in mass skincare

Primary Benefits: Reduces sebum, antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory
Side Effects: Rarely causes issues; very well tolerated
Key Interactions: Pairs with niacinamide for enhanced oil control
Notes: Zinc PCA is zinc salt of pyrrolidone carboxylic acid — sebum regulating + healing

Primary Benefits: Fades hyperpigmentation, treats acne and rosacea, anti-inflammatory
Side Effects: Mild tingling; itching on sensitive skin (usually temporary)
Key Interactions: Can combine with niacinamide; compatible with most actives; gentle enough for daily use
Notes: Available OTC 10–15%; prescription at 15–20% (Finacea). Safe during pregnancy unlike retinol

Primary Benefits: Kills acne-causing bacteria, reduces inflammatory acne, unclogs pores
Side Effects: Dryness, peeling, bleaches fabric
Key Interactions: Do NOT combine with retinol (deactivates it); use separate from vitamin C; follow with barrier cream
Notes: 2.5% as effective as 10% with fewer side effects. Rinse-off formulas for sensitive skin

Primary Benefits: Signals skin to produce collagen, firms skin, reduces fine lines, repairs barrier
Side Effects: Very low risk; well tolerated
Skin Types: Mature, Dry, All types seeking anti-aging
Key Interactions: Do NOT mix with AHA/BHA (can degrade peptides); pair with niacinamide and hyaluronic acid
Notes: Types: signal peptides (Matrixyl), carrier peptides (copper), neurotransmitter-inhibiting (Argireline)

Primary Benefits: Fades stubborn melasma and PIH, brightens skin, very gentle
Side Effects: Rare; generally well tolerated; occasional mild irritation
Key Interactions: Can combine with niacinamide, azelaic acid, vitamin C; mild alternative to kojic acid
Notes: Rising star for hyperpigmentation; 2–5% OTC; comparable to hydroquinone without the risks

Primary Benefits: Inhibits melanin production, fades dark spots, safer alternative to hydroquinone
Side Effects: Low risk; mild irritation in rare cases
Key Interactions: Pairs with niacinamide and vitamin C for enhanced brightening
Notes: Derived from bearberry plant. Converts to hydroquinone slowly — safer profile

Primary Benefits: Calms inflammation, promotes wound healing, strengthens barrier, anti-aging
Side Effects: Very rare; may cause contact allergy in sensitive individuals
Key Interactions: Pairs well with ceramides, hyaluronic acid, niacinamide
Notes: Key actives: madecassoside, asiaticoside, asiatic acid. Popular in Korean skincare

Primary Benefits: Hydrates, repairs, fades scarring and pigmentation, anti-aging
Side Effects: Rare; some may react to animal-derived ingredient
Key Interactions: Combines well with hyaluronic acid, niacinamide
Notes: Active components: glycoproteins, enzymes, hyaluronic acid, copper peptides, zinc

Primary Benefits: Inhibits melanin production, fades dark spots and melasma
Side Effects: Skin irritation; potential contact dermatitis with prolonged use; photosensitizing
Key Interactions: Can boost with vitamin C; do NOT mix with strong AHAs
Notes: Derived from fungi; unstable — look for stable formulations. Limited OTC %

Primary Benefits: Mimics retinol (boosts collagen), gentler; treats acne, fades dark spots
Side Effects: Very well tolerated; rare mild irritation
Skin Types: Sensitive, Pregnant, All types avoiding retinol
Key Interactions: Can be combined with retinol to boost effects; pairs with rosehip oil, vitamin C
Notes: From Psoralea corylifolia seeds. Growing evidence base but smaller than retinol

Primary Benefits: Exfoliates, brightens, anti-bacterial; good for darker skin tones (less risk of PIH)
Side Effects: Mild; gentler than glycolic; slight photosensitivity
Skin Types: All types; especially Sensitive and Darker skin tones
Key Interactions: Compatible with niacinamide; avoid AHA stacking for beginners
Notes: Largest AHA molecule — slowest penetration, gentlest. Good starter acid for darker skin

Primary Benefits: Powerful antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, anti-aging, protects from environmental damage
Side Effects: Rarely causes irritation
Skin Types: All types; especially Mature and Urban skin
Key Interactions: Pairs with ferulic acid and vitamin E for enhanced antioxidant protection
Notes: Found in grapes/berries; unstable — choose stable formulations

Primary Benefits: Antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, reduces acne
Side Effects: Irritation, contact dermatitis at high concentrations; must be diluted
Key Interactions: Do NOT use undiluted; pairs with aloe for soothing; caution with other actives
Notes: 1–5% is effective OTC range; avoid eye area

Primary Benefits: Lightweight moisturizer, non-comedogenic, balances oil, anti-aging
Side Effects: Very well tolerated; rare allergy
Key Interactions: Excellent vehicle for active delivery; pairs with all actives
Notes: Plant-derived (olive, sugarcane) or shark-derived. Stabilized form of squalene

Primary Benefits: Draws moisture to skin, maintains barrier, softens skin
Side Effects: Rare; very well tolerated
Skin Types: All types; especially Dry and Dehydrated
Key Interactions: Pairs with all ingredients; foundational humectant
Notes: Simple, effective, inexpensive. Concentration 1–10% in most products

Primary Benefits: Stabilizes vitamin C and E, doubles antioxidant protection, anti-aging
Side Effects: Mild irritation in sensitive skin
Skin Types: All types; especially Mature and UV-exposed
Key Interactions: Essential pairing with vitamin C + E; boosts SPF protection
Notes: Does not work effectively alone — usually formulated with C+E (e.g., SkinCeuticals CE Ferulic)

Primary Benefits: Holds more water than HA (4–5x), plumps, reduces transepidermal water loss
Side Effects: Very well tolerated
Skin Types: All types; especially Dry and Dehydrated
Key Interactions: Can replace or layer with hyaluronic acid; compatible with all actives
Notes: Derived from fermented soybeans (natto). Forming moisture film over HA layer

Primary Benefits: Prevents UV damage, aging, skin cancer, hyperpigmentation worsening
Side Effects: Some chemical filters cause irritation; mineral (zinc oxide, titanium dioxide) gentler
Key Interactions: Apply last in AM routine; reapply every 2 hrs; neutralizes many active benefits without it
Notes: Mineral (physical): zinc oxide, titanium dioxide. Chemical: avobenzone, tinosorb, etc.
